newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bank of France injects 14.9 bln Ffr at tender.
newsitem.headline: Bank of France injects 14.9 bln Ffr at tender.

text.p: The Bank of France injected 14.9 billion francs at a securities repurchase tender held on Wednesday to allocate funds for injection into the money market on Thursday.
It accepted bids for 56.0 billion francs in new liquidity, 14.9 billion more than the 41.1 billion leaving the market on Thursday when a previous pact expires. The new pact expires on July 16.
The Bank of France said the tender was being held a day earlier than usual to take into account the repayment of the so-called Balladur bond, maturing on July 16.
A Bank of France spokeswoman said the larger than usual size of the injection did not indicate there had been any change in monetary policy.
She said the extra liquidity was needed for several technical reasons, including the impact of the expiry of the Balladur bond, but declined to elaborate further.
The Bank of France said it allocated 17.0 billion francs to bidders offering Treasury bills as collateral, satisfying 5.4 percent of such demand.
It allotted a further 39.0 billion to bidders putting up private paper, satisfying 16.5 percent of this demand.
